printer.profile.title: Printer
printer.profile.body: The printer you will print on. Its build volume is drawn as a box, and every part shows whether it fits.
printer.profile.tip: A part that doesn't fit needs one more cut. Fit to Printer, which cuts automatically, comes in phase 2.

printer.volume.title: Show printer volume
printer.volume.body: Draws the build volume of the chosen printer around the selected part.
printer.volume.tip: Green box: the part fits. Red box: it's too big.

parts.list.title: Parts
parts.list.body: Every model and every piece you cut appears here. The selected part is the one tools work on.
parts.list.tip: Untick the checkbox to hide a part. Double-click to rename, Del to delete. Cut a piece again to keep splitting it step by step.

cut.axis.title: Cut direction
cut.axis.body: The axis the cutting plane faces. Z cuts horizontally (top/bottom), X and Y cut vertically.
cut.axis.recommended: Z for most figures: flat cut faces print cleanly and are easy to glue.
cut.axis.tip: Fine-tune with Tilt, or drag the 3D handle in the viewport.

cut.tilt1.title: Tilt (first axis)
cut.tilt1.body: Rotates the cutting plane around the first axis perpendicular to the cut direction, in degrees.
cut.tilt1.recommended: 0° unless the seam should follow a natural line of the model.
cut.tilt1.tip: Angled cuts can hide seams along clothing, hair or armour edges.

cut.tilt2.title: Tilt (second axis)
cut.tilt2.body: Rotates the cutting plane around the second perpendicular axis, in degrees.
cut.tilt2.tip: Combine both tilts to place the plane at any angle.

cut.offset.title: Position
cut.offset.body: Moves the plane along its direction, in mm, measured from the part's center. The orange line in the viewport is exactly where the cut will be.
cut.offset.tip: Avoid cutting through very thin areas (fingers, weapons): leave room for pins later.

cut.center.title: Center
cut.center.body: Puts the plane back through the middle of the part with no tilt.

cut.keep.title: Keep
cut.keep.body: Which side(s) to keep after cutting. "Side the arrow points to" is the side the plane's normal arrow points at.
cut.keep.tip: Keep one side to trim off a base or a support plinth.

cut.gizmo.title: 3D handle
cut.gizmo.body: Shows a draggable plane in the viewport. Drag the plane to move it, drag the arrow to rotate it. The numbers update automatically.

cut.apply.title: Cut
cut.apply.body: Cuts the selected part with the plane. Both new pieces are closed solids (the cut faces are filled), so they are printable right away.
cut.apply.tip: Select one of the new pieces and cut again to split step by step. Very large models take a few seconds; the window stays responsive and Cancel stops it.

repair.analyze.title: Analyze
repair.analyze.body: Checks if the model is a closed, printable solid: holes, flipped normals, non-manifold edges, duplicates and floating pieces.
repair.analyze.tip: Every opened file is analyzed automatically.

repair.merge.title: Merge distance
repair.merge.body: Vertices closer than this distance are joined. This closes tiny cracks where two surfaces almost meet.
repair.merge.recommended: 0 (only exact matches). Try 0.001–0.01 mm if the report shows many small holes.
repair.merge.tip: Large values can collapse fine detail.

repair.degenerate.title: Remove degenerate faces
repair.degenerate.body: Deletes zero-area triangles (all three corners on a line or point). They confuse slicers and booleans.

repair.duplicates.title: Remove duplicate faces
repair.duplicates.body: Deletes triangles that appear twice. Duplicates cause non-manifold edges.

repair.debris.title: Remove floating debris
repair.debris.body: Deletes tiny separate pieces (smaller than 0.25% of the model size), usually leftover junk from modelling.
repair.debris.tip: Real small parts (eyes, gems) are much larger than this limit and are kept.

repair.orientation.title: Fix normals
repair.orientation.body: Makes every triangle face outward and consistently oriented. Inner walls of hollow models correctly stay facing inward.

repair.holes.title: Fill holes
repair.holes.body: Closes open gaps in the surface so the model becomes watertight.
repair.holes.recommended: On. Phase 5 adds smooth curved filling for big holes.

repair.max_hole.title: Max hole size
repair.max_hole.body: Only fills holes with at most this many edges. All fills every hole.
repair.max_hole.tip: Limit it if the model has an intentional big opening you want to keep.

repair.apply.title: Auto Repair
repair.apply.body: Runs every enabled repair step in the right order, then re-analyzes the model.
repair.apply.tip: Clean models only cost an analysis; nothing is changed if nothing is wrong.

repair.show_edges.title: Show problem edges
repair.show_edges.body: Draws hole borders and non-manifold edges in red on the model, so you can see where the problems are.

export.folder.title: Export folder
export.folder.body: Where the STL files are saved. Each part becomes one file named after the part.
export.folder.tip: Rename parts in the list first (for example head, body, arm_left).

export.selected.title: Export selected part
export.selected.body: Saves the selected part as a binary STL in millimetres, at full resolution.

export.all.title: Export all visible parts
export.all.body: Saves every part that is ticked in the list, one STL per part.
export.all.tip: In Elegoo SatelLite you can import all files at once and arrange them on the plate.

export.check.title: Warn before exporting
export.check.body: Asks before saving parts that haven't passed the printable check.

printer.edit.title: Edit printers
printer.edit.body: Add your own printers with their build volume, type (resin or FDM) and the free margin kept around parts.
printer.edit.tip: The type sets the default pin and joint tolerances in the Connect tools.

parts.merge.title: Merge (union)
parts.merge.body: Fuses the selected parts into one closed solid. Overlapping and touching parts become one piece, for example two halves of a cut.
parts.merge.recommended: Use for parts that should print as one piece.
parts.merge.tip: Needs closed solids; if it refuses, run Auto Repair first.

parts.combine.title: Combine
parts.combine.body: Puts the selected parts into one part without fusing them. Fast, and works for any parts.
parts.combine.tip: Good for exporting several pieces as one STL file.

parts.delete.title: Delete
parts.delete.body: Removes the selected parts. Ctrl+Z brings them back.

move.offset.title: Move
move.offset.body: Moves the selected parts along X, Y or Z in millimetres. You can also drag the part in the 3D view (Shift + drag moves it up or down).
move.offset.tip: Slicers re-place parts anyway; moving is for arranging pieces, molds and checking fit.

move.rotate.title: Rotate
move.rotate.body: Rotates the selected parts around their center, in degrees (first X, then Y, then Z).
move.rotate.tip: Use Lay flat to put a chosen face exactly on the bed.

move.rotate90.title: Rotate 90°
move.rotate90.body: Turns the parts a quarter turn around that axis.

move.on_bed.title: Put on the bed
move.on_bed.body: Lowers or raises the parts so their lowest point is exactly at Z = 0, computed on the full-detail model.
move.on_bed.recommended: On, before exporting parts for printing.

move.centered.title: Center on the bed
move.centered.body: Moves the parts so the middle of their bounding box is at X = Y = 0.

move.lay_flat.title: Lay flat
move.lay_flat.body: Click a face of the part: it is turned so that face lies flat on the bed. Ideal for cut faces, which print best flat on the plate (FDM) or angled with supports (resin).

move.scale.title: Scale
move.scale.body: Uniform size in percent. 100% keeps the original size.
move.scale.tip: Scaling changes pin and wall sizes too; add connectors after scaling.

move.reset.title: Reset
move.reset.body: Throws away the move that is not applied yet.

move.apply.title: Apply
move.apply.body: Applies the move to the full-detail parts. It is also applied automatically when you switch tools. Ctrl+Z undoes it.

cut.mode.title: Cut type
cut.mode.body: Plane: one flat cut. Grid: several planes at once. Curve: along a line you draw. Free-form: along a bendable surface.
cut.mode.tip: Curved and free-form seams can follow natural lines of a figure (clothes, hair) so they hide better.

cut.fit.title: Fit to printer
cut.fit.body: Calculates the fewest pieces so every piece fits the chosen printer (with its free margin), also trying a 90° turn on the bed. The planes are spread evenly.
cut.fit.tip: Move a plane in the list so the seam avoids faces or fine details.

cut.grid_planes.title: Planes
cut.grid_planes.body: All cutting planes of the grid. Select one to change its position.

cut.grid_pos.title: Plane position
cut.grid_pos.body: Position of the selected plane along its axis, in mm.

cut.grid_count_help.title: Pieces along an axis
cut.grid_count_help.body: How many pieces along this axis. The planes are spread evenly; fine-tune them in the list.

cut.curve_draw.title: Draw the cut line
cut.curve_draw.body: Starts drawing: click points on the model in the 3D view. The view switches to a flat projection so the line cuts exactly where you see it.
cut.curve_draw.tip: Shift+click for a sharp corner, Backspace removes the last point, Enter finishes.

cut.curve_undo.title: Remove last point
cut.curve_undo.body: Deletes the last point of the line (same as Backspace).

cut.curve_smooth.title: Smooth curve
cut.curve_smooth.body: Draws a smooth curve through the points. Off: straight segments (a stepped or zigzag cut).
cut.curve_smooth.recommended: On for organic shapes, off for stepped joints.

cut.free_size.title: Control grid
cut.free_size.body: Number of control points per side (3×3 to 8×8). More points allow more detailed shapes.

cut.free_height.title: Point height
cut.free_height.body: How far the selected control point lifts the surface from the base plane, in mm. You can also drag the point in the view.
cut.free_height.tip: Points only move along the plane's normal, so the two pieces can always be pulled apart.

cut.free_reset.title: Flatten
cut.free_reset.body: Puts all control points back on the base plane.

cut.gap.title: Joint gap
cut.gap.body: Removes a thin layer between the two pieces of a curved cut so they slide together after printing.
cut.gap.recommended: Resin 0.05–0.1 mm, FDM 0.15–0.2 mm. 0 when you will glue the pieces.

conn.find.title: Find joint
conn.find.body: Finds the flat face two selected parts share (for example the two halves of a cut). Runs by itself when you select two parts.

conn.pick.title: Pick flat face
conn.pick.body: Click a flat face of one part to put connectors on it alone, e.g. magnet holes in a base, or when the other part is in another file.
conn.pick.tip: Do the same on the other part with the same settings so the holes match.

conn.type.title: Connector type
conn.type.body: Dowel: separate pin, holes in both parts. Peg: pin grown on one part. Magnet / metal rod: holes for parts you buy. Square key: stops turning. Tongue & groove: rim all around. Dovetail: sliding wedge rail.
conn.type.recommended: Resin figures: 2–3 dowels or a tongue & groove. Big FDM parts: dowels or brass rods.

conn.magnet.title: Magnet size
conn.magnet.body: Common disc magnets (diameter × thickness). The hole is made bigger by the gap per side and deeper by the extra depth.

conn.size1.title: Diameter / width
conn.size1.body: Size of the pin, peg, rod or magnet; for a key its side, for a tongue its width, for a dovetail its narrow width at the face.
conn.size1.recommended: Dowels 3–5 mm for figures, 5–8 mm for big FDM parts.

conn.size2.title: Length / height
conn.size2.body: Dowel or rod: total length (half goes into each part). Peg, key, tongue, dovetail: how far it sticks out. Magnet: its thickness.

conn.edge.title: Distance from edge
conn.edge.body: How far the tongue or dovetail stays inside the outline of the joint face.
conn.edge.tip: In thin hollow walls the tongue is centred in the wall automatically.

conn.flare.title: Side angle
conn.flare.body: How much the dovetail widens towards its top. More angle holds better but needs more material.

conn.angle.title: Direction
conn.angle.body: Turns the selected key or the dovetail rail (all of them if none is selected). The dovetail slides in along this direction.

conn.male.title: Male side
conn.male.body: Which part gets the peg, key, tongue or rail; the other part gets the matching hole, groove or channel.
conn.male.tip: Put the male side on the part that is easier to print with it, e.g. the bottom part.

conn.fit.title: Fit
conn.fit.body: How tight the parts go together. Press: tight, no glue. Snug: holds, leaves room for glue. Slide: easy to assemble. Loose: very easy.

conn.clearance.title: Gap per side
conn.clearance.body: Space left between mating surfaces, on each side (a 4 mm pin with 0.1 mm gets a 4.2 mm hole). Set by the printer type and fit; change it freely.
conn.clearance.recommended: Resin 0.05–0.15 mm, FDM 0.15–0.3 mm. Best: print the tolerance coupon.

conn.depth_gap.title: Extra hole depth
conn.depth_gap.body: Holes are made this much deeper than needed, so glue, resin overcure or a drooping layer cannot stop the parts from closing.

conn.chamfer.title: Chamfer
conn.chamfer.body: Bevels pin tips and hole mouths so they find each other easily and elephant foot does not block them.

conn.wall.title: Minimum wall
conn.wall.body: Material kept around every hole. Connectors are placed only where this fits; red dots break the rule.

conn.count.title: Per contact area
conn.count.body: How many connectors each separate contact area gets (a cut through two legs has two areas).
conn.count.recommended: 2 (one would let the parts turn, unless it is a key).

conn.auto.title: Place automatically
conn.auto.body: Spreads the connectors evenly where they fit with the minimum wall. You can then drag them.

conn.add.title: Add by clicking
conn.add.body: While on, each click on the joint face adds a connector there. Click an orange dot to select it, drag it to move it.

conn.clear.title: Clear
conn.clear.body: Removes all connectors from the face.

conn.boss.title: Solid boss
conn.boss.body: In hollow models the wall is often too thin for a hole. A solid column is then added inside, joined to the wall, and the hole goes into it. It never pokes out of the outside surface.

conn.coupon.title: Tolerance coupon
conn.coupon.body: Makes a small test plate with 5 holes (from a little tighter to a little looser than the current gap) and a matching pin. Hole k is marked with k dots.
conn.coupon.tip: Print it with the same resin, settings and orientation you will use for the model.

conn.best.title: Best hole
conn.best.body: After printing the coupon, enter the hole where the pin fits the way you want and press Use this gap. It is saved for this printer and fit type.

conn.apply.title: Add connectors
conn.apply.body: Cuts the holes and adds the pegs to the full-resolution parts. Problems (a hole breaking through a wall) are reported. Undo works as usual.

mold.thickness.title: Silicone thickness
mold.thickness.body: The gap between the model and the shell, filled with silicone. It is the same everywhere and exact to a few micrometres.
mold.thickness.recommended: 3–5 mm for small figures, 5–10 mm for big or heavy parts.

mold.wall.title: Shell wall
mold.wall.body: Thickness of the printed shell. It only has to hold the soft silicone in shape.

mold.quality.title: Quality
mold.quality.body: Size of the voxels used to build the shell surfaces. Finer is smoother but slower and needs more memory. The silicone thickness is exact at every quality; only the smoothness of the shell changes.
mold.quality.recommended: Normal; Draft to try ideas quickly.

mold.base_z.title: Base height
mold.base_z.body: Height of the base plane: the mold is open here and stands on the base plate. Normally the bottom of the model (Model bottom).
mold.base_z.tip: Lower it and turn on the rod for a model without a flat bottom.

mold.plate.title: Base plate
mold.plate.body: A plate the model and the shell stand on. The shell's lower edge sits in a groove of the plate, which seals the silicone and aligns the shell.

mold.plate_margin.title: Plate margin
mold.plate_margin.body: How far the plate reaches beyond the shell (and its flanges).

mold.groove.title: Groove depth
mold.groove.body: How deep the shell's edge sits in the plate. The groove is wider than the wall by the fit gap.

mold.locator.title: Model pocket
mold.locator.body: A shallow pocket in the plate matching the model's footprint, so the model goes back to exactly the same place.

mold.rod.title: Rod
mold.rod.body: A rod from the plate up to the lowest point of the model, for models that do not stand on a flat bottom. Glue the model onto it.

mold.split.title: Two halves
mold.split.body: Splits the shell in two so it can be opened to take the cured silicone out. The halves get flanges with bolt holes and alignment keys.

mold.angle.title: Parting direction
mold.angle.body: Direction of the parting plane, in degrees around the vertical axis. By default the plane runs along the longer side of the model.
mold.angle.tip: Choose a direction where no part of the model wraps around the shell's halves.

mold.offset.title: Parting offset
mold.offset.body: Moves the parting plane sideways from the middle of the model.

mold.flange.title: Flanges
mold.flange.body: Rims along the parting line of both halves, for bolts or clamps.

mold.bolt.title: Bolts
mold.bolt.body: Bolt holes through both flanges, spread evenly along them (M3: 3.4 mm, M4: 4.5 mm holes).

mold.nuts.title: Nut traps
mold.nuts.body: Hexagon pockets on one half so the nuts cannot turn.

mold.keys.title: Alignment keys
mold.keys.body: Small pegs on one half's flange and matching holes on the other, so the halves always close the same way.

mold.sprue.title: Pour hole
mold.sprue.body: Where the silicone is poured in, by default the highest point of the cavity (orange dot). Drag the dot to move it.

mold.chimney.title: Tube height
mold.chimney.body: How far the pour and vent tubes stick out of the shell. Silicone rising in them shows the mold is full.

mold.funnel.title: Funnel
mold.funnel.body: A cone on top of the pour hole for easier pouring.

mold.vents.title: Vents
mold.vents.body: Thin tubes at the places where air would be trapped (blue dots): high points of the cavity other than the pour hole. Find vents places them automatically.

mold.add_vent.title: Add / remove vents
mold.add_vent.body: While Add vent is on, click on the model where a vent should go. Select a dot and press Remove to delete it.

mold.feet.title: Feet
mold.feet.body: Posts on top of the shell that all end at the same height: turned over for casting, the mold stands level on them.
mold.feet.tip: They are made taller than the pour and vent tubes.

mold.density.title: Silicone density
mold.density.body: Used to turn the volume into grams (see the silicone's data sheet).

mold.preview.title: Preview
mold.preview.body: Updates the coarse preview (it also updates by itself when you change a setting).

mold.build.title: Build mold
mold.build.body: Builds the mold at the chosen quality and adds the parts (two halves and the base plate) to the list. The silicone thickness is measured on the result.

decal.place.title: Place on the model
decal.place.body: Press it, then click on the model where the centre of the decal should go. The frame lies on the surface there, with image up following the world Z axis. Drag the orange dot afterwards to slide it over the surface.
decal.place.recommended: Turn the model so you look straight at the spot first.

decal.text.title: Text
decal.text.body: The typed text becomes the decal. Persian and other right-to-left scripts are joined and ordered correctly. The frame is fitted to the letters.
decal.text.recommended: For resin, letters at least 0.4 mm wide and 0.3 mm high print cleanly.

decal.font.title: Font
decal.font.body: Any font installed on the computer. Bold letters have thicker strokes, which print better when small.
decal.font.recommended: Bold, simple fonts for small text.

decal.image.title: Image
decal.image.body: A PNG, JPG or BMP picture. As a logo, the dark parts on a light background are used (or the opaque parts of a picture with transparency). As a texture, brightness is the height, like a height map.
decal.image.recommended: High contrast black-and-white images for logos; up to 1600 pixels are used.

decal.mode.title: Raised or pressed in
decal.mode.body: Raised adds material on top of the surface. Pressed in carves the image into the surface.
decal.mode.recommended: Pressed in is safer on thin walls of hollow models only if the wall is thicker than the depth plus 1 mm.

decal.depth.title: Height / depth
decal.depth.body: How far the image rises out of the surface or goes into it, measured along the surface, so it is the same on curved parts.
decal.depth.recommended: 0.4–1 mm for resin, 0.6–1.5 mm for FDM.

decal.kind.title: Image use
decal.kind.body: Logo / text gives a flat top and steep sides. Texture uses every shade of grey as a height, for patterns like leather, scales or stone.
decal.kind.recommended: Logo for text and symbols, texture for surfaces.

decal.threshold.title: Threshold
decal.threshold.body: For logos: the brightness where the image counts as on. Lower it to make thin lines thicker, raise it to make them thinner.

decal.invert.title: Invert
decal.invert.body: Swaps the on and off parts: for text, the plate around the letters is raised and the letters stay low.

decal.blur.title: Smooth
decal.blur.body: Softens the image before it is used (in pixels of the image). Removes noise in photos and makes texture reliefs gentler.
decal.blur.recommended: 0 for logos; 1–3 for textures from photos.

decal.tile.title: Repeat
decal.tile.body: Repeats the image this many times across and down the frame, for patterns.

decal.size.title: Size
decal.size.body: Width and height of the frame on the surface, in mm. With Keep proportions the height follows the width so the image is not stretched.

decal.rotation.title: Rotation
decal.rotation.body: Turns the image around the surface normal, in degrees.
decal.rotation.recommended: 0° keeps image up pointing to world up.

decal.projection.title: Projection
decal.projection.body: Flat projects the image straight onto the surface. Wrap bends it around a cylinder (bottles, arms, columns) so it is not stretched at the sides. The radius is measured from the surface when set to 0.
decal.projection.recommended: Wrap for round parts when the decal covers more than a quarter of the way around.

decal.detail.title: Detail
decal.detail.body: Size of the voxels used to build the relief. Smaller is sharper but slower and needs more memory.
decal.detail.recommended: Normal (0.1 mm) for most decals, Fine (0.05 mm) for small text on resin.

decal.apply.title: Apply decal
decal.apply.body: Builds the relief and joins it with the part (or carves it out). The part is replaced; Undo brings the old one back.
decal.apply.recommended: Check the preview from a few sides first.
